messages.author: 829edb046441d165
messages.subject: strange result from PSCBS
parts:
Hi Henrik ,

I have really strange result from PSCBS.
What I did were doCRMAv2 ->extractPSCNArray->compute copy number -> dropSegmentationOutliers -> segmentByPairedPSCBS-> plotTracks.

But I found that one of my sample does not have any minor/major CN nor DH. See attachment. I have checked BAF values. There are non-NA values.

what do you think there is going on?

Br,
C.Y

messages.author: 829edb046441d165
messages.subject: Re: strange result from PSCBS
parts: Additionally, the total copy number analysis shows the plot looks ok.

What I did were doCRMAv2 ->extractPSCNArray->compute copy number -> dropSegmentationOutliers -> segmentByPairedPSCBS-> plotTracks.

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: strange result from PSCBS
parts:
DH is only defined from heterozygous SNPs. If you don't see any DH
signals, that indicates that none of the SNPs where called
heterozygous. This could be an indicatation of a failed or a very
noise normal sample.

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: strange result from PSCBS
parts:
It is difficult for me to say whether it is failed or the normal sample is nose. Can you have a look at these four figures ? They are from two paired tumor samples. One of them is missing DH . In the other sample, minor cn is 0 and major cn is 1. I am also attaching the total copy number estimate.

Br,
Chengyu

heterozygous.  This could be an indicatation of a failed or a very
noise normal sample.

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: strange result from PSCBS
parts:
Hi, it's not easy to say. My point is that you look at the normal
data, i.e. BAF (but also TCN relative to a global reference), you may
have more clues on the quality of the normal sample. If that is bad,
then then tumor-normal TCN is most likely bad too.
